question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

We waited for him **since two hours.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**since two hours**" is incorrect because "**since**" is used to denote a specific point in time (e.g., since 2 PM, since Monday) and not a duration.
 
• When referring to a duration of time, the correct preposition to use is "**for**."
 
• The correct phrase should be "**for two hours**," which indicates the length of time we have been waiting.
 
• Thus, the error lies in the inappropriate use of "**since**" in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"We waited for him **for two hours**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "until two hours"** – This is incorrect because "**until**" refers to a point in time and is not used to describe a duration.
 
• **Option 2: "from two hours"** – This is incorrect because "**from**" is generally followed by the starting point of an action, not a duration.
 
• **Option 3: "by two hours"** – This is incorrect because "**by**" indicates a deadline or end point, not the duration of an action.
